body.text: Fri, 18 Sept, 7:50 pm, Final score, Tigers 0, Raiders 6
NRL grand final live: Roosters thrash Broncos in NRLW decider before Knights-Roosters men's grand final
The Newcastle Knights will have a home crowd in Sydney for the NRL grand final against the Roosters after thousands of fans made the trip down the M1.
Earlier, the Roosters won their third NRLW premiership, scoring seven tries to thrash the Brisbane Broncos 30-6 in a blowout and exact revenge in a rematch of the 2025 decider.
The win sealed an undefeated season for the Roosters, whose halfback Tarryn Aiken won the Karyn Murphy medal for best on field.
Follow all the action in our live blog below, check out all the stats in the full NRLW and NRL grand final ScoreCentres, and tune in to our live radio coverage.

Brigginshaw breaks down
Broncos coach Scott Prince, captain Tamika Upton, and retiring legend Ali Brigginshaw have just spoken to the media, following their heavy defeat.
Brigginshaw had red eyes, and couldn't contain her emotions, in what is a tough end to one of the greatest NRLW careers.
"I've played in many football games where the result hasn't gone our way," she said before breaking down in tears, unable to continue.
Prince jumped in and praised on the veteran saying she's "a bloody legend."
Upton also credited the legacy Brigginshaw has left for the club.
"She's left us in really good hands... what she's done for myself personally, the confidence she gives you as a person, as a player, I think that's what she gives you," she said.
Brigginshaw re-grouped and said she's eager to remain working in rugby league, and she hopes to earn selection for the Jillaroos' squad for the upcoming Rugby League World Cup.
And as she left the room, she remarked to a room full of journalists:
"We've done press conferences with one person in here, so we've come a long way."
When it came to dissecting the game itself, Prince said the number of errors his side made ultimately hurt them.
"They're a great footy team and so are we, but in big games you need a bit of luck," he said.
"We had a few opportunities to build some pressure, and we didn't execute.
"They're a great football team... and you have to play well to beat a team like the Roosters.
Goodbye to Mark Nawaqanitawase
Speaking of departing players, one of the game's best, Mark Nawaqanitawase, is heading back to the 15-a-side game immediately after this season.
The former Wallabies winger, who has 11 caps to his name in union, has a two-year contract with Japanese rugby side Saitama Wild Knights to go to after this match.

His return to union is a huge boost to the code in a World Cup year, but there's nothing saying that the three-code international (he also represented the Australian 7s team at the Paris Olympics) won't be back in league after his contract is over, perhaps as soon as the 2028 season.
Will he sign off with a premiership?
Or just another freakish try.

Newy Found Glory
The Knights haven't played in a men's grand final since 2001, so a lot has happened since then.

In fact, 11 of the 21 players named in Newcastle's squad for this evening's grand final, including halves Fletcher Sharpe and Sandon Smith, weren't even born when Andrew Johns led his Knights past the heavily favoured Parramatta Eels 25 years ago.
Since that title, their second in five years, it's been a bumpy road for Newcastle.

Andrew Johns's premature retirement accompanied a second-last finish in 2007 and they bounced in and out of the finals for almost the next decade, leading to three straight wooden spoons from 2015 through 2017.

Kalyn Ponga's arrival from North Queensland in 2018 heralded a new generation and coach Adam O'Brien arrived two years later. They reached the finals in four of his first five seasons, always in the bottom half of the eight, before the nadir came with a fourth last-placed finish from 11 seasons.
During the year, the team signed Dylan Brown for a record $1.5 million-a-season deal. By the end of the season O'Brien was axed.

Former Titans coach and Roosters assistant Justin Holbrook arrived along with Brown and the team hit the ground running in Las Vegas with a team retooled around Brown, Ponga and Fletcher Sharpe, turning the league's worst attacking team into one of the most exciting outfits in the game.
Why is Connor Watson out?
The Roosters suffered a huge blow this week after Connor Watson was ruled out of the game.
The hooker suffered a head knock just one minute after coming on to the field in the preliminary final victory over the Dolphins on Friday.
Watson had hoped to play, and tried to overturn the mandatory 11-day stand down period for category one concussions.
However, that was denied and so, nine days after his head knock, Watson has to miss out.

"Ultimately it came down to protocol and we stand by that," coach Trent Robinson said. "Connor spoke to the group quite clearly about 'this is about the group' and he passed that on, and then the player who took his spot in the 19, Benaiah spoke about the love for Connor and what it means for his role coming into the team and that's what teams are about."
"Ultimately it came down to protocol and we stand by that," coach Trent Robinson said.

"Connor spoke to the group quite clearly about 'this is about the group' and he passed that on, and then the player who took his spot in the 19, Benaiah spoke about the love for Connor and what it means for his role coming into the team and that's what teams are about."
That being said, had Watson been allowed to play it would have been a scandal of epic proportions.

The reasons for the 11-day stand down are very clearly there to protect players from further neurological damage, and despite the somewhat loose and lenient interpretation of the game's laws during finals often allowing players to play despite foul play taking place, that simply cannot be allowed to be the case when the health of a player is at risk.
Nevertheless, a big blow for Watson, in what is his last game for the club.
He will join St George Illawarra next season before linking up with the PNG Chiefs in 2028.

Key Event
Grand final team news
Here are the final teams for tonight's match.
Roosters
No late changes for the Roosters.
Benaiah Ioelu joined the six-man bench on Friday when Connor Watson was ruled out on concussion protocols.
Daly Cherry-Evans will become the oldest player to play in a grand final, aged 37 years and 183 days.
He overtakes Melbourne Storm legend Cameron Smith, who was 37 and 130 days old in his last decider.
Knights
One change for the Knights, and it's at the problematic hooker spot.
Phoenix Crossland was suspended for the hip drop that broke Nathan Cleary's leg, so Thomas Cant starts the game at hooker in the 19 jersey, with Harrison Graham remaining on the bench.
Kyle McCarthy joins the six-man interchange.
Newcastle is heaving
ABC's Bridget Murphy is out and about in Newcastle, where fans have been filling pubs around the city since long before midday, and there's an air of excitement and anticipation.
The Knights' home ground Hunter Stadium is open to the public tonight, and 22,500 people have reserved tickets to watch the men's decider. A big night ahead for Novocastrians...
Julia Robinson is just about inconsolable
The Broncos winger has been one of the best big-game players for a long time, but she battled today, like most of her teammates.
"We wanted to give Ali [Brigginshaw] a good game to send her off the way she deserved, so obviously a bit sad," Robinson tells ABC Sport.
Robinson is weeping as the conversation turns to Brigginshaw's legacy.
"She's a true leader, on and off the field, she's the heart of the Broncos, she's going to be this legacy that carries on for generations.
"She's going to be missed, missed by the team, missed by everyone, but she'll still be around and make a big impact on the rugby league community.
"I'm so grateful I had the opportunity to play with Ali, she's one of the greats."
The Roosters are back on top of the NRLW!
Roosters skipper Isabelle Kelly hails Ali Brigginshaw
Isabelle Kelly makes sure to shout out the Broncos...
"You set the standard for this comp as well I know every time we play each other there's respect."
And Ali Brigginshaw...
"I've been so lucky to play with and against you. What you've done for this game is truly incredible."
And, of course, Corban Baxter and Millie Elliott, particularly as mums raising the next generation of Roosters...
"It's created such a special bond for us all to look forward to for years going forward."
Key Event
Tamika Upton pays tribute to victims of Knights parade crash
Broncos captain and former Knights fullback Tamika Upton starts her speech mentioning the victims of the horrible incident at the Newcastle Knights' parade yesterday.
"I want to acknowledge the families of the tragedy in Newcastle," Upton says.
"On behalf of the Broncos and myself, sending best wishes to the community."
And she hails the premiership-winning Roosters as the standard all NRLW teams are chasing.
"You guys are incredible. It's no coincidence you're up here doing what you're doing."
Key Event
Tarryn Aiken wins her second Karyn Murphy Medal!
The Sydney Roosters halfback pulled all the strings in this victory, just as she did back in 2024, and is rightly rewarded.
As she makes her way up to the stage, I think I hear a "Newcastle" chant go up. Expect more of that later tonight.
Very different days for three NRLW greats
Ali Brigginshaw is in tears as she speaks to Channel Nine, while former teammate Millie Elliott is beaming (although there may be a few tears of joy in there too).
"Thank you to everyone who's supported me and been there for me. I've had an incredible career but it's only thanks to those people," she tells Nine.
"Thanks to Ali Brigginshaw and Corban Baxter for all they've done, they were paying this game long before me."
Baxter pays tribute right back to her great mate on ABC Sport.
"We've been really tight knowing we're going to retire all season, Millie's just the best human so it's been great to go out with her."
"It hasn't really sunk in yet, I'm feeling all the feels right now," Baxter adds.
"I love playing footy, I love all the girls, I'm going to miss it so much."
Key Event
The Roosters get their NRLW premiership back!
The Sydney Roosters have won their third NRLW premiership with a dominant performance and a 30-6 win over great rivals Brisbane.
This one truly feels like revenge for last year and finally they complete the perfect 13-0 season to send Millie Elliott and Corban Baxter out in fitting fashion.
"I love this team so much, they really deserve this," Elliott says.
69' The Broncos challenge to get a rest
The Broncos are caught on the last as Sariah Paki wraps up Shannon Mato.
Tamika Upton challenges, but I think it's just to let her teammates suck in some deep breaths.
